title: Explicit, Implicit, and Scattered: Revisiting Event Extraction to Capture Complex Arguments
research_question: How should event argument extraction be reformulated and benchmarked when important event arguments may be implicit in context or distributed across multiple discontinuous parts of a discourse rather than appearing as one explicit span?
methodology: The authors create DiscourseEE from Reddit discussions about medications for opioid use disorder, selecting three event types and defining 41 argument roles across core, type-specific, subject-specific, and effect-specific categories. They annotate 396 post-comment pairs with 7,464 argument annotations using eight locally recruited annotators who received four weeks of training; at least two annotators produced arguments for each sample and a third reviewer resolved disagreements, yielding mean relaxed-match inter-annotator F1 of 0.811. Event argument extraction is reformulated as natural-text generation rather than span extraction, and extractive QA, generative FLAN-T5 models, and several zero-shot LLMs are benchmarked using relaxed-match and exact-match F1 measures on train/validation/test splits of 246/50/100 samples. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1turn945402view2

key_findings.finding: A majority of annotated event arguments require more than ordinary contiguous-span extraction: 51.2% are implicit and 17.4% are scattered, so 68.6% are either inferred or distributed across the discourse. citeturn326926view0turn568280view2

The paper demonstrates a fundamental limitation of exact evidence-span assumptions: implicit arguments have no directly stated source span, while scattered arguments are assembled from discontinuous information distributed through the document. citeturn568280view1turn945402view3
key_findings.section: 2 Event Extraction via Text Generation; 7 Related Work

key_findings.finding: Because the dataset stores generated natural-text argument values rather than start/end text spans, it supports semantic event reconstruction but does not itself provide strict provenance spans for every extracted argument. citeturn945402view0turn945402view2
key_findings.section: 2 Event Extraction via Text Generation; 5.2 Argument Extraction Models

key_findings.finding: Traditional extractive QA performs substantially worse on complex arguments, with mean relaxed-match F1 of 17.13 and recall of only 9.40% for implicit and 13.44% for scattered arguments. citeturn568280view2turn326926view3

Even the strongest evaluated generative system remains far from solving the task: GPT-4 with question-guided prompting reaches mean relaxed-match F1 of 41.98, while its best reported recall for implicit arguments is 36.53% and for scattered arguments is 54.12%. citeturn326926view3turn945402view3

Exact-match scoring can mark semantically correct generated arguments as wrong, and the authors' qualitative analysis indicates that exact-match evaluation therefore underestimates generative extraction quality. citeturn568280view4turn945402view3

The annotation process itself shows that scattered and implicit arguments create substantial human difficulty, including missed distributed evidence and the need for deeper contextual inference. citeturn326926view5

For the workplace-action research question, the paper contributes a useful representation of implicit and scattered arguments but does not study workplace communication or explicitly model action owners, deadline-to-action binding, conditional obligations, or negated obligations. Its ontology instead concerns health-advice events. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1

limitations: DiscourseEE is based on health-advice discourse from Reddit rather than workplace email or enterprise chat, so transfer to organizational action and decision extraction is untested. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1
Only 396 post-comment pairs were fully argument-annotated, although they contain 7,464 argument annotations. citeturn568280view5

Annotation is expensive and difficult to scale because annotators must generate argument values rather than select spans and because implicit and scattered arguments require substantial contextual reasoning. citeturn568280view5turn326926view5

Relaxed-match F1 depends on a manually selected semantic-similarity threshold, while exact-match F1 substantially underestimates semantically equivalent generations; the paper therefore lacks a fully satisfactory evaluation metric. citeturn945402view0turn568280view5
The benchmark assumes the ground-truth event type for the event-argument extraction experiments, simplifying the end-to-end extraction problem. citeturn945402view2

Models were evaluated with common zero-shot prompts rather than individually optimized prompts, so the reported LLM results are benchmarks rather than model-specific upper bounds. citeturn945402view2turn945402view3

Because the annotations are natural-text values rather than source offsets, the dataset is not directly suitable for applications requiring exact evidence-span provenance without an additional grounding layer. citeturn945402view2
The ontology does not contain explicit workplace constructs for owner assignment, deadlines attached to actions, conditional duties, or negated obligations.
raw_claims: DiscourseEE contains 7,464 annotated event arguments from online health discourse. citeturn326926view0
The fully annotated portion contains 396 post-comment pairs. citeturn945402view1
About 51.2% of the arguments are implicit and 17.4% are scattered. citeturn326926view0
The authors define implicit arguments as information not directly mentioned but inferable from context. citeturn568280view0turn945402view3
Scattered arguments combine information appearing in multiple parts of a discourse rather than one contiguous span. citeturn568280view0turn945402view3
The dataset uses natural-text argument annotations instead of start and end offsets for argument spans. citeturn945402view2
Eight annotators received four weeks of training for the complex argument-annotation task. citeturn326926view2turn945402view1
Each annotated sample was handled by at least two annotators and reviewed by a third annotator. citeturn326926view2
The extractive QA baseline obtained a mean relaxed-match F1 of 17.13. citeturn568280view2turn326926view3
GPT-4 with question-guided prompting achieved the highest reported mean relaxed-match F1 of 41.98. citeturn326926view3
Implicit arguments remained particularly difficult, with the strongest reported implicit recall reaching 36.53%. citeturn326926view3

Exact matching substantially reduces measured performance for scattered arguments because generated wording and structure can differ from the reference while retaining the same meaning. citeturn326926view6turn945402view3
The authors publicly provide the dataset, evaluation resources, and code. citeturn568280view6
The study does not directly address workplace owner assignment, action deadlines, or obligation polarity.
